model_prior_familiarity.description: The question evokes the well-known Card and Krueger New Jersey/Pennsylvania minimum-wage fast-food study. Prior memory includes qualitative controversy and difference-in-differences setting. No remembered coefficient or published table will be used as a result.

search_exposures.search: Card Krueger 1992 New Jersey fast food raw data codebook data.dat; New Jersey minimum wage April 1992 official history
search_exposures.exposure: Search snippets disclosed 410 restaurants/two survey waves, the qualitative slight employment increase, target authors/title. No published numeric treatment coefficient exposed.

search_exposures.search: site.davidcard.berkeley.edu data minimum wage public.dat codebook; author data page
search_exposures.exposure: Data page supplied target title/outlet/year and njmin.zip route. Unopened teaching-code search snippet showed raw parsing approach (46 names/trailing empty column) and later reanalysis abstract snippet mentioned negative estimates and t-ratios <=0.7 in other samples. These results are excluded from the analysis.

Unopened GitHub replication search result exposed a reported +2.75 coefficient, supporting specification descriptions and sample counts 351/357. These are excluded from numerical construction and original code was not inspected. This constitutes numeric target-answer contamination.

numerical_source_rule: Only project-code estimates from downloaded raw data enter results.
design_exposure_qualification: Raw preparation and supporting specification descriptions (gap, controls, 0.4/0.6 part-time weights, no managers) appeared in unopened search-result snippets before design lock. They were not code-copied, but choice of supporting checks cannot be claimed uncontaminated. Primary estimator, complete-component rule and pair sample arise directly from raw codebook and independent computation.
